entries.subject: feat(changelogs): derive structured per-change explanations from commit bodies
entries.body:
Auto (git) entries previously rendered with `changes: []` — only the
admin-curated DB rows had per-change bullets. Now every auto commit gets
a structured `changes[]` derived in `mapRawCommitsToEntries`, so each
card explains itself change-by-change instead of as one body blob.

Derivation has two sources, in priority:

  A. Commit body bullets / paragraphs (`parseChangesFromBody`). Lines
     starting with `-` / `*` / `•` / `N.` / `N)` / `a.` each begin a
     change; multi-line continuations fold into the current bullet. When
     the body has no markers, each blank-line-separated paragraph becomes
     one change. Intro lines before the first bullet are context (already
     in the summary) and dropped.

  B. File-area fallback (`deriveChangesFromFiles`). When the body yields
     nothing (terse one-liner / empty), the touched files are grouped by
     area — `src/app/(admin)/insights/games/...` → "Insights / Games",
     `src/lib/queries/...` → "Queries" — and one change per area is
     emitted, ordered by churn. Guarantees EVERY commit carries at least
     one explanatory line. Verified against current history: 65/80
     commits derive from the body, the remaining 15 all resolve via the
     file-area fallback (none left blank).

Each change's `kind` is inferred from keywords (fix/bug → fix; add/new →
feature; perf/faster → improvement; remove/drop → breaking;
refactor/chore/docs → infra; default improvement) so the existing
per-kind bullet icons light up. Capped at 8 changes/commit (renderer
shows the overflow). Trailer-stripping (Co-Authored-By etc.) is shared
with the summary path via an extracted `stripTrailers`.

The mapper now also carries scope / files / additions / deletions
through to the entry. loadJsonEntries reads the richer JSON shape (all
fields optional, narrowed defensively via narrowFiles / finiteOrNull) so
an older committed JSON still parses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: feat(changelogs): capture per-file + scope + additions/deletions in commit data pipeline
entries.body:
The auto-entry (git commit) cards previously carried only a
files-changed COUNT and the commit subject/body. To support per-change
explanations + a Files disclosure, the data pipeline now captures the
full shape per commit.

generate-changelog.mjs runs TWO `git log` passes and merges them by SHA:

  1. --name-status → per-file STATUS letter (A/M/D/R/…) + path,
     plus subject/body/iso.
  2. --numstat     → <added>\t<deleted>\t<path> per file.

Git applies only ONE diff-output format per invocation (--name-status,
--numstat, and --shortstat are mutually exclusive — the last wins), so a
single pass cannot yield both the status letter AND the +/- counts.
Rather than guess a status from numstat (12\t0\tx is ambiguously add or
modify), status comes from pass 1 and counts from pass 2, joined on
(sha, path). Both passes are local + build-time so the doubled cost is
negligible.

Also dropped `-z`: with -z the diff formats switch to NUL-delimited path
output which collides with the inter-record NUL and shatters the file
list. Records are now delimited by a leading %x1e (ASCII RS) in the
pretty-format instead, so the multi-line body block can't be mistaken
for a new commit; fields stay %x1f-delimited.

Per-commit captured: filesChanged (TRUE count, pre-cap so the renderer
can show "+N more"), additions, deletions, scope (conventional-commit
(scope) parse), and files[] (path + status + per-file additions/deletions,
capped at 20).

The runtime GitHub list-commits path gets the same shape for parity:
scope is parsed from the subject (free), but additions/deletions/files
stay null/[] because the list endpoint omits per-commit stats and
following N detail links would blow the rate limit.

ChangelogEntry + ChangelogFile types gain the new fields, all OPTIONAL
so the admin-curated DB path and older committed JSON still parse.

entries.subject: feat(changelogs): visible data-source chip + admin diagnostics for GitHub API path
entries.body:
`/changelogs` silently fell back to the build-time JSON snapshot whenever
the GitHub REST call didn't return entries (missing token, wrong branch,
401/403/timeout, etc.), so a stale "Last published 13h ago" was
indistinguishable from a live feed.

`getAutoChangelogEntries()` now returns an `AutoChangelogResult` envelope
carrying `source` (`"github"` | `"json"` | `"json-fallback"`), the
resolved `branch`, `lastFetchAt`, `lastError`, and `tokenConfigured`.
The Last published KPI tile renders a green "Live (GitHub)" chip when
the API responded and an amber "Snapshot (build-time)" chip otherwise,
with the failure tag in the tooltip.

An admin-only collapsible diagnostics panel below the entries lists
token state, resolved branch + repo, last-fetch ISO, current source,
last-error tag, and cache TTL so a stale tile can be debugged from the
page without env-var spelunking.

Cache key for the GitHub fetch now includes the resolved branch
(`["changelog-github-v1", branch]`) so changing `CHANGELOG_GIT_BRANCH`
invalidates immediately instead of serving the previous branch's
entries for up to 60s.

feat(changelogs): real-time commit history via GitHub API (JSON is fallback)
entries.body:
The /changelogs page surfaced a stale "Last published" timestamp because
auto-entry cards were baked into `src/lib/changelog/recent-pushes.json`
at BUILD time by `scripts/generate-changelog.mjs` (wired as `prebuild`).
Two failure modes resulted:

  1. Production deploys from `main`. Commits pushed to a feature branch
     (e.g. `claude/hungry-gould`) didn't appear in prod until the branch
     merged AND a fresh deploy landed.
  2. Even on the deployed branch, a commit pushed after the last Vercel
     deploy didn't show up until the next build refreshed the JSON.

Adds `src/lib/changelog/github.ts` with a server-only
`getLatestCommitsFromGitHub()` helper that hits the GitHub REST
`/repos/{repo}/commits` endpoint at REQUEST time and returns the same
shape the JSON does. Reads:

  - `GITHUB_TOKEN`            (required to enable the live path)
  - `CHANGELOG_GIT_BRANCH`    (default "main")
  - `CHANGELOG_GIT_REPO`      (default "PackyGG/pokewin-admin")

`getAutoChangelogEntries()` in `src/lib/queries/changelog.ts` now tries
the GitHub source first (wrapped in `unstable_cache` 60s, tag
`"changelog"`) and falls back to the build-time JSON if the token is
missing, the API call fails, or the network is unreachable. The JSON
path remains fully functional — the prebuild script still writes it
on every build, just as a safety net rather than the primary source.

Both sources flow through a shared `mapRawCommitsToEntries()` helper
so the rendering logic stays in one place. Conventional-commit subject
filters (drop tsc/lint/wip/fixup/squash noise) are duplicated in
`github.ts` so the live API path produces the same card set the JSON
would (modulo freshness).

Other notes:

  - The author label on each auto card now reads `CHANGELOG_GIT_BRANCH`
    (default "main") instead of the hardcoded "claude/hungry-gould"
    label that ended up in the JSON path. This way the same code path
    works on whichever branch the deploy is built from.
  - The "Last published" tile's Info tooltip now explains the live vs.
    fallback distinction so a stale tile during fallback mode is
    explicable instead of looking like a bug.
  - The `scripts/generate-changelog.mjs` header comment now documents
    that the JSON is a fallback source.
  - No new dependencies — uses Node 20+ built-in `fetch` with a 5s
    AbortController timeout. Token only needs `repo:read` scope; we
    never mutate GitHub. The token is server-only (file is
    `import "server-only"`) and passed via Authorization header, never
    a query parameter. The list endpoint is hit at most once per 60s
    per server, well under the 5000/hr authenticated rate limit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.body:
The per-type breakdown popover (previous commit) shows WHICH ledger
types drive the headline GGR, but not WHO. When the dashboard reads
"GGR = -$102k" and the popover surfaces "rakeback_claim = $89k", the
next question is "and which users got that $89k?". This expander
answers it.

same window/type set as the headline GGR (real_users CTE applies the
staff+blacklist filter UP-FRONT so per-user totals match the
aggregate), sorted by ABS(net) DESC so the loudest movers in either
direction surface first. Each row links to /users/<id> for one-click

— admins kept asking "is this number right?" with no way to verify it
themselves. The reconciliation popover attempted in 8e1e835 (round 5)
was reverted because the GGR→P&L bridge it surfaced was structurally

the residual was meaninglessly large.

show GGR's OWN components. The popover lists every wager-side ledger
type (pack_opening / battle_bet / etc.) and every payout-side type
(battle_refund / rakeback_claim / card_sale / etc.) with the summed
ABS(amount) for the selected period. Bottom of the popover shows the
math literally — wagersTotal − payoutsTotal = GGR — which equals the
headline aggregate by construction (same SQL filter, same wager+payout
type sets, same staff/blacklist exclusion).

driving it. No more "is this a bug or real?" cycles.

  sweep over ledger_transactions, splits the result into wager /
  payout buckets via the canonical type sets from

entries.subject: feat(changelogs): richer auto entries — surface commit body as summary + files-changed chip
entries.body:
Auto entries (one per git commit) previously rendered title-only because
`scripts/generate-changelog.mjs` captured `%h|%aI|%s` and the query
helper hard-coded `summary: ""`. That made them look thin next to
admin-curated cards with paragraphs + bullets.

Changes:

- Script now uses `git log -z --shortstat --pretty=format:'%h\x1f%aI\x1f%s\x1f%b\x1f'`.
  NUL is the between-record separator; `\x1f` (ASCII unit separator) is
  the within-record field separator. This sidesteps the "commit body
  contains a pipe / newline" parsing pitfall the previous pipe-based
  format had to dodge with "split on first two pipes only" logic.
- `--shortstat` adds "N files changed, M insertions(+)..." per commit;
  parsed into `filesChanged: number | null` per entry.
- `getAutoChangelogEntries` reads the new `body` / `filesChanged`
  fields and surfaces them through the existing `ChangelogEntry`
  shape. Added `filesChanged?: number | null` to the shared type
  (optional, so older committed JSON without the field still parses).
- `normalizeCommitBody` strips RFC-style trailers (Co-Authored-By,
  Signed-off-by, Reviewed-by, Fixes:, Closes:, …), collapses 3+ blank
  lines into a paragraph break, and caps at 3 paragraphs with a "…"
  marker so a verbose commit can't swallow the feed.
- New `<ChangelogSummary>` client component handles the long-text
  collapse: estimates rendered lines from the cleaned text, clamps
  to ~5 lines with a "Show more / Show less" toggle when the summary
  exceeds the threshold. Short summaries render inline without the
  toggle.
- New files-changed chip ("3 files") on auto-entry cards, sourced
  from the shortstat parse. Hidden on curated entries where the
  concept doesn't apply.
- Regenerated `src/lib/changelog/recent-pushes.json` with the new
  fields populated for all 80 entries (run via `--force`).

No new dependencies. tsc + next lint clean.

entries.subject: revert(dashboard): drop GGR -> P&L reconciliation popover -- couldn't make math reconcile
entries.body:
The bridge 'P&L approx= GGR - inventoryDelta - voucherDelta' added in
8e1e835 is not a true accounting identity. GGR is wagers - payouts
(restricted ledger types); house P&L is deposits - withdrawals -
balanceChange - inventoryDelta - voucherDelta. Substituting the
balanceChange definition into the P&L formula yields:

  P&L = GGR - cardWithdrawals - (rainPrizes + rakeback + creatorTips +
        racePrizes + leaderboardPrizes + gifts + bonuses + cardSales +
        battleRefunds + ...) - inventoryDelta - voucherDelta

i.e. the popover was missing card withdrawals AND every non-GGR-typed
credit category. At the time of the report the popover showed a $92k
residual on a $4.6k 'P&L' line -- user correctly flagged it as
nonsense.

Switching the inventory valuation to cards.price (Path A in the spec)
would not have fixed it because the residual is structurally driven by
the missing terms above, not by inventory valuation drift. It would
also have made the popover's inventoryDelta line inconsistent with the
rest of the codebase, which values inventory at
user_inventory.value_at_obtained everywhere (lifetime PnL snapshot,
per-user PnL, windowed PnL, daily PnL, period PnL breakdown, pack /
battle pure PnL).

Restored GgrStatCard to its pre-8e1e835 shape (no Popover, no
Reconciliation row helper, no Info icon import). Dropped
inventoryDeltaPeriod / voucherDeltaPeriod from the dashboard stats
payload -- they had no other consumers. The underlying
windowedPeriodDelta query is kept because realizedPnlPeriod still
needs inventoryChangePeriod / voucherChangePeriod for its own
calculation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: fix(cards): correct per-set count cache key + report Pokemon set state
entries.body:
The `getCardsStats(setId)` query was wrapped in `unstable_cache` with a
static `keyParts = ["cards-list-stats-v2"]`. Function arguments are NOT
automatically mixed into the keyParts — they only segment cache slots
explicitly. So calls with different `setId` values collided on the same
cache slot: whichever landed first served every subsequent request,
producing the "Cards in Pokemon: 65" symptom against an actual 50,588
catalog (or vice versa) when the catalog-wide and Pokemon-tab variants
were both hit within the 60s window.

Fix: bind `setId` into keyParts per call ([..., setId ?? "all"]) so each
tab has its own cache slot. Extracted the inner aggregate logic into
`fetchCardsStats` to keep `getCardsStats` thin.

entries.subject: fix(users): wire sort headers for Role / Status / # Deposits + deterministic tie-break
entries.body:
Three related fixes for "sort buttons at the top of /users not returning
sorted rows":

1) Role / Status / # Deposits column headers were plain string labels,
   not <UsersSortHeader />. Clicking them did nothing, so admins who
   tried "show me banned users at the top" or "rank by deposit count"
   got the default created_at-desc list back and assumed sort was broken.
   All three now render the same sort-button component the other numeric
   columns use, with up/down arrow indicators that reflect the active
   sort.

2) The server query whitelist didn't know about depositCount or status:
   - depositCount → added to rawSqlSorts; a conditional JOIN counts
     completed deposit ledger txs only when this sort is active so the
     COUNT(*) groupBy isn't paid on every list query.
   - status → added a dedicated compound Prisma orderBy on
     [is_banned, is_locked, id] since the computed status string isn't
     a real column.

3) Every Prisma-path orderBy now ends in `{ id: "asc" }` as a
   deterministic tie-breaker. Without it, sorting by Balance / Deposited
   / Wagered would return the handful of non-zero users in the right
   order, then a long tail of $0-balance users in arbitrary
   Postgres-internal order across page navigations — which is exactly
   the "rows not in expected sorted order" the user reported.

Client-side comparators in sort-context match: depositCount, role
(admin > support > creator > user) and status (banned > locked > active)
sort the currently visible page optimistically while the server refetch
is in flight.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: feat(dashboard): GGR → P&L reconciliation popover — surfaces inventoryΔ + voucherΔ gap
entries.body:
The headline GGR card and the Daily P&L chart diverge by design
(wager/payout vs balance-delta math). Admins kept reading this as a bug
because the dashboard never showed where the gap comes from.

Adds an inline info trigger on the GGR card that opens a small popover
with the three-line bridge for the SELECTED period:

  GGR
  Inventory Δ   (user-held card value growth, drag on house P&L)
  Voucher Δ     (unclaimed voucher growth, drag on house P&L)
  ──────────
  ≈ P&L

inventoryDelta / voucherDelta come from the windowedPeriodDelta query
that already powers realizedPnlPeriod — no new SQL, just exposes the
two deltas in the dashboard payload. Labelled "≈ P&L" because the full
P&L formula also nets deposits − withdrawals − ledger balance change,
so a small residual is expected (and surfaced as a footer hint when
non-trivial).

entries.subject: feat(sets): force-absorb-into-Pokemon admin action + button
entries.body:
The initial seed (`seedInitialSets`) only moved cards with NULL set_id
— the ~50k legacy TCGPlayer-import cards kept their old set_id and
stayed scattered across dozens of import sets.

Adds a second-stage bulk action that sweeps EVERY card not in the
OnePiece set into Pokemon, then deletes the now-empty legacy sets in
a separate cleanup pass. Both steps audit-logged independently
(`cards_force_absorbed_into_pokemon` for the move, `empty_legacy_sets_
deleted` for the cleanup), gated by a new `__can_force_absorb_cards`
capability so it can be granted distinctly from `__can_seed_initial_sets`.

The Pokemon / OnePiece set IDs are looked up by name so the action is
fully idempotent: cards already in Pokemon are no-op writes, cards in
OnePiece are skipped by the NOT clause, and a re-run on a clean
catalog deletes zero legacy sets.

entries.subject: fix(cards): explicit select in getCards/getCardDetail so schema drift can't crash the list
entries.body:
Both queries used findMany/findUnique without an explicit select clause,
which makes Prisma ask the database for every column the generated
client knows about. When a newly-added schema column (e.g. the
OnePiece-only `cost` / `power` columns from a865aa8) hasn't reached
the live DB yet, the query 500s and the whole card catalog renders
the safeQuery fallback ("Couldn't load this section").

Switching both queries to an explicit select listing only the columns
the UI actually renders eliminates that schema-drift vulnerability —
the query will never ask for `cost` / `power` for the list / detail
surfaces, because neither surface displays them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
